STEP 1 - Scene: Looks like a snack or side of cut avocado pieces on a white paper/foam plate, photographed from directly above on a wooden board setup.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White plate roughly 20 cm in diameter (side-plate size). Area = 3.14 x 10^2 = 314 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Three wedges of ripe avocado (flesh visible, skin removed or partly peeled). No dressing or oil visible.

STEP 4 - Area: Wedge 1 (top) about 6% of plate; wedge 2 (middle) about 6%; wedge 3 (bottom) about 7%. Total about 19% of the vessel covered.

STEP 5 - Volume: Each wedge is roughly 10 cm long, 4 cm wide, 2.5 cm thick at the fattest point, so about 15 to 20 ml each. Gross volume of the three pieces is roughly 55 ml total (area about 60 cm^2 x about 1 cm average height, in the outer envelope of the pile).

STEP 6 - Grams: Avocado flesh is dense, so use about 0.9 g/ml for the solid pieces (bulk density for dense fruit pieces is higher than cut vegetables). 55 ml x 0.9 ≈ 50 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Avocado is about 160 kcal per 100 g. 50 g x 1.6 ≈ 80 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Three avocado wedges totaling about 50 g and about 80 kcal is plausible for what is visible. A half avocado weighs around 100 g, and these pieces look like about a half-avocado's worth of flesh in total, so 50 g is reasonable, perhaps slightly low. I'll keep 50 g.
